description: OpenHydroNet is Google Research's open implementation of the riverine forecasting architectures used in Google FloodHub. It extends NeuralHydrology with forecast-sequence models, including a masked mean-embedding LSTM and an earlier state-handoff LSTM. Inputs are catchment attributes, weather forcing, streamflow training targets and model configuration; outputs are discharge forecasts and evaluation metrics. The documented application is global river forecasting, while a trained configuration determines catchment coverage and forecast steps. Source is free under Apache-2.0, with training and evaluation instructions. External forcing and training datasets have separate terms. A limitation is that the repository is not an officially supported Google product, and local accuracy requires evaluation, especially where inputs are missing. Discharge forecasts can inform flood-risk analysis for water and transport assets; they are not inundation-depth maps. NeuralHydrology (platform-neuralhydrology) is the related parent software. No training data or checkpoint was downloaded.
